sprites.name: bird_body
sprites.notes: Redrawn in v4.28 as concept B1 "Rondine" -- a deep forked tail, sickle wings swept back, a small head and a short beak. The canvas, the origin and the call site are v4.26's: 51x21 CANVAS_PIXELS, **flap axis canvas row 15**, blitted at BIRD_SPRITE_ORIGIN_Y_PX -15 and mirrored about that row for the down-stroke. What changed is legibility at the 42 px the bird actually reaches: v4.26's "Colomba" raised both wings forward, and at that size the two humps were the largest shape in the outline and read as a fanned tail, so the eye turned the animal round. The facing was never wrong -- v4.27 measured that and `bird-facing` pins it -- so nothing here is mirrored; the largest shape simply moved behind the head. Head and beak point +x, the only direction birds drift.

sprites.name: cloud_body
sprites.notes: Redrawn in v4.26 as concept C1 "Batuffolo": one mass of four large round lobes over a wide low base, with no cut edge and no second sheet. Its tone is a single vertical ramp inside the one shape (white at the crown to #DEDEDE at the base) and the silhouette is feathered by a 1.5-unit Gaussian blur, so the edge is a passage of alpha rather than a line. A cloud is atmosphere, not an object standing on the ground -- DESIGN_NOTES 4.1 -- which is what lets it carry a gradient. Canvas and content box unchanged, so CloudCoverage.CLOUD_CONTENT_HALF_UNITS still reads 133.

The v4.25 back (#4A6A84) sat at CIELab dE 5.2 from the water in its worst case and vanished at night and in a storm; it is now #A19A9C at dE 26.1. Faces +x, the only way lake decorations drift. v4.31 cropped the 4x6 px of leading padding the redraw left inside the canvas -- 345x174 to 342x168 -- and compensated DOLPHIN_ORIGIN_X/Y_UNITS by the (1, 2) units removed, to (-56.3, -27); no drawn pixel moved. This note used to claim the v4.26 content was placed so the old (-57.3, -29) still landed the animal on its leap point. Measured in v4.31: it does not, and did not. The content centre is (57.167, 28.0) units and the origin puts it (+0.87, +1.0) units off the leap point. Moving the animal onto it is an artwork decision, open as item 105.

sprites.name: ground_flowers_bloom
sprites.notes: One clump of ground flowers in bloom: tulip, daisy, buttercup, bluebells and cosmos on a single canvas, so a scatter of them is one blit per clump rather than one per bloom. The blooming half of the ground_flowers pair -- ground_flowers_dry is the same clump gone over, and the renderer picks between them from the seasonal palette. Neither is named for a season: the dry one serves autumn and winter both. Fixed art -- the user gets ON and OFF and no colour, because a meadow that follows a theme's building tint is a meadow of the wrong flowers. Every head is two cut papers, an ink shadow offset 0.55 units under a light paper, which is the v4.32 buildings' shadow grammar.

sprites.name: ground_flowers_dry
sprites.notes: One clump of ground flowers gone over: thistle, coneflower, goldenrod, a spent aster, a grass spike and a seed head. Same canvas and same blit origin as ground_flowers_bloom, so the two are interchangeable at the call site. Drawn for autumn AND winter -- dry stems standing out of snow are a real thing to look at, and calling this sprite _autumn would have been a lie every time the winter palette was on. Fixed art, same reason as its twin. Chosen whenever the seasonal palette is AUTUMN or WINTER; flowersEnabled still only says whether there are flowers at all.

sprites.name: palmtree_fronds
sprites.notes: The coconut palm's living crown, redrawn from scratch in v5.1 from concept A "Cocco". Seven broad lens-shaped blades that arch and fall, each a card with its own paper shadow and a lighter fold along its back, and three coconuts under the convergence. The canvas is 56x48 units because the blades fall BELOW the attachment point, which the 40x40 canvas this replaces had no room for. Its two alternatives share this canvas and this origin.

sprites.name: palmtree_fronds_dead
sprites.notes: Halloween's palm crown: the same seven blades collapsed and folded back down the trunk, two stumps still up, in straw browns. A whole crown on palmtree_fronds' canvas with the same declared attachment, so drawPalmTree blits it at the same origin in place of the live one. Its content sits low in the canvas because a fallen crown occupies less of it; cropping to the ink would move the sprite. Fixed art in the straw browns for the same reason tree_dead_branches is: a dead frond is not a theme colour.

sprites.name: palmtree_fronds_frost
sprites.notes: The winter palette's palm crown: the same seven blades in a cold green with snow settled along the backs of the five upper ones. v5.1 made it a WHOLE CROWN rather than the five white caps that used to be blitted on top of the live one, so drawPalmTree draws it INSTEAD of palmtree_fronds and the pixel-for-pixel coverage condition the overlay needed is gone. Same canvas, same declared attachment. Snow is white over a #C9D6E0 card, the two papers house_small_roof_snow.svg cuts it from.

sprites.name: palmtree_trunk
sprites.notes: The coconut palm's trunk, v5.1: a curved spindle leaning 7 units right over a flared foot, crescent leaf scars up the front, a shadow band down the right flank and a strip of light down the left. ANCHORED ON ITS FOOT, WHICH IS DECLARED RATHER THAN DERIVED. The drawn content spans x 2..60 px while the foot's centre is at x 24 px, because the trunk leans -- CONTENT_BOTTOM_CENTRE, true of the straight trunk this replaces, would derive 31 and stand the palm more than two units beside its own ground shadow while pivoting its sway off its base. drawPalmTree blits at (-8, -58), which is this anchor negated. The canvas is what `normalize` leaves: two pixels of guard on each side, because a filtered blit reads the column beside the ink and clamping onto it changes the edge (v4.31).
